landing.h1Pre: The moment for AI is now.
landing.h1Em: Doing it well is not obvious.
landing.sub: Between 70% and 85% of enterprise AI projects fail to deliver expected value. The cause is rarely technology — it is method. This platform turns the methodology used by YourBrand consultants into a guided, optionally supervised assessment your organization can complete in weeks instead of months.

landing.modulesSub: From strategic alignment to sustained value capture. End-to-end, vendor-agnostic, regulation-ready and engineered around the points where most initiatives actually fail.

modules.d: Maturity diagnosis across 5 dimensions, value-vector prioritization, risk appetite.
AI-readiness questionnaire by area, heat map, weighted value/effort matrix.
Two-horizon portfolio (Quick Wins + transformational), AI Committee, 12-metric dashboard.
Rules vs. classical ML vs. GenAI: decision tree, multi-criteria scoring, structured questionnaire.
Sales, marketing, customer service, finance, HR, operations, supply chain, legal/compliance.
Technical lifecycle (5 phases with gates) + adoption (fear of replacement, XAI, Shadow AI).
Operating model, governance, talent, continuous improvement of the portfolio.

landing.diffSub: Not slideware theory. Every module ships with templates, gates, dashboards and questionnaires you use in workshop, not in the showcase.

diff.d: Decisions are driven by criteria, not by a partner’s preferred stack. The right tool for the right problem.
Questionnaires, scoring matrices and weighted criteria replace gut feel and political negotiation.
Fear of replacement, Shadow AI, XAI visual design, human-AI workflow patterns, trust calibration.
Aligned with UK GDPR, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001 and OECD principles from day one.
Technical implementation and human adoption run in parallel from day one. Never sequentially.
Each module ships with templates, gates, dashboards and questionnaires ready for workshop use.

assistant.title: YourBrand Assistant
assistant.sub: AI in the context of your assessment · indicative answers
assistant.welcome: Hi Max 👋 I’m your AI assessment assistant. I can help you understand questions, prioritize areas, compare your readiness with benchmarks, or summarize your progress. Where shall we start?
suggested: How far along am I in the assessment?
Compare my readiness with the manufacturing sector
assistant.tip: I’m most useful while you’re answering the questionnaire and you’re unsure how to score. Ask me about a specific question and I’ll explain the spirit of the metric with examples.
assistant.escalate: Hand this off to a human consultant

replies.progress: You’re at {{pct}}% of the overall assessment. So far you’ve answered {{answered}} of 132 questions across the Maturity diagnostic (M1) and the area kits. The most advanced areas are **Customer Service (100%)** and **Sales B2B (78%)**. I suggest finishing M1 before opening new areas — the maturity score calibrates every recommendation downstream.
replies.prioritize: Based on what you’ve answered so far and your profile (mid-size UK manufacturing, focus on efficiency), I would prioritize in this order: **1) Customer Service** — already complete, high pain × high readiness, clear Quick Win with ticket RAG. **2) Sales B2B** — solid readiness, predictive lead scoring is an obvious Quick Win. **3) Operations** — high impact but low readiness, invest in sensors first. HR and Legal can wait.
replies.catalog: An "accessible data catalog" measures whether a new analyst can find the key data sources **in minutes, not weeks**, with no special permissions and no need to ask colleagues. **Level 5**: active catalog with lineage, owners, definitions and search. **Level 3**: scattered documentation that requires context. **Level 1**: nobody knows where the data is until they ask. If your organization is between 1 and 2, this is probably your first job before starting serious AI work.
replies.benchmark: Mid-size UK manufacturers (250-2,000 employees) typically sit at **Level 2-3 on average** (Repeatable→Defined), with the biggest gaps in **Culture (1.8/5)** and **AI process (2.1/5)**. Your current 2.9 score is just above average. Companies that break past 3.5 invariably share: (1) a formal Center of Excellence, (2) 3+ cases in production, (3) 12+ months of formal portfolio execution. It’s an 18-24 month conversation, not a quarter.
replies.default: Good question. Let me check your assessment context… Based on what you have so far, I would suggest: (1) finishing the Data block in M1 before judging your overall readiness, (2) attaching at least one piece of evidence per block so the diagnosis is defensible, and (3) if this is about a specific answer, mark it with "I don’t know" so a consultant can review it with you.

reviewNotes.title: Calibration M1 · Culture
reviewNotes.body: Suggesting E2 drops from 4 to 3: the organization tolerates technical failure but penalizes project failure.

reviewNotes.title: Validation · Sales · Enablers
reviewNotes.body: ICP flagged as gap. Recommend closing it before starting the lead scoring case.

validatedChapters.title: M1 · Maturity diagnostic
validatedChapters.note: Overall calibration OK. Lowered Culture from 2.4 to 2.0 — the organization tolerates technical failure but penalizes project failure, which constrains experimentation. Global score adjusted from 2.9 to 2.7. I recommend investing in quality gates and a per-role training plan before larger initiatives.

validatedChapters.title: M2/M5 · Sales B2B
validatedChapters.note: Lead scoring stands as priority Quick Win, validated. ICP must be closed before starting the case — I marked it as a prerequisite. Conversational intelligence also launches, but only after legal approves consent-based recording.

validatedChapters.title: M2/M5 · Customer Service
validatedChapters.note: Ticket RAG is the case with the highest expected ROI in the whole portfolio. Data in good shape, motivated team, KB up-to-date. I recommend launching a pilot in 4 weeks with 30% of volume and clear FCR and CSAT metrics.

validatedChapters.title: M2/M5 · Finance & Administration
validatedChapters.note: Payment anomaly detection requires cleaning the supplier master file first (12% duplicates). I left it as a prerequisite before the pilot. Monthly close is a lower-risk Quick Win — recommend starting there.

validatedChapters.title: Final consolidated report
validatedChapters.note: Executive report ready and validated. The 6 identified Quick Wins could generate an estimated 3.4× return in 18 months if executed in the proposed order. Next step is presenting to the steering committee in a 90-min session to validate priorities and funding.
